page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.8-32 is a compute-oriented virtual machine instance within the Standard flexible family. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6987C-P processor operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. It features 8 dedicated physical cores and 16 virtual CPUs (vCPUs) with 2 threads per core, coupled with 32.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

The instance configuration does not include bundled local storage disks, requiring external block volumes for persistent operating system and data storage needs. In addition, there are no hardware acceleration devices or GPUs present on this instance type. Network provisioning includes one complimentary public IPv4 address assigned to the virtual machine.

With its clock frequency of 3.9 GHz and a 1:2 ratio of compute threads to memory, the VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.8-32 exhibits resource characteristics designed for compute-bound operations rather than memory-heavy caching. The absence of integrated local storage shifts I/O responsibilities to remote block storage infrastructure. This balance makes the instance appropriate for batch compute processing, CI/CD pipelines, web application serving, and distributed microservices requiring dedicated CPU cycles without excess memory overhead.
